Guards best of the three.

what: How a weapon fights, on its item card (pack, loot, shops)

what: How a weapon fights, on its item card (pack, loot, shops)

Hew, before the attack lesson
text: There, see, they're at the boots again, it's *always* the boots first with them, I don't know why. And don't stop at one knock, mind. I watched a lad do that once, and _it got up_.

what: Hew, before the block lesson
text: Well, there's three of them now, and that's too many to go rolling about between, so you stand your ground and let them knock. And that's *my* kiln they're pissing on, the little sods.

what: Hew, before the dodge lesson
text: See that one, how it's crouching? When they get down low like that they're coming *straight through you*, shield or no shield, and there's no stopping them. Best not be standing there when it arrives, is all.

what: Hew, reaching his hut
text: That's ^home^, kettle's older than you are. Hang on, I *didn't* leave that door open.

what: Hew's last words to you
text: Get the count to Odric, stray, Father Odric, he'll be wanting it.

what: Hew, if you talk to him mid-lesson
text: Ask me later, stray, once you've got your breath back. I'll ~still be talking~, don't worry.

what: Hew, when more looters come
text: There's _more of them_ in the trees, stray, and they're coming this way.

what: Hew, on where the goblins went
text: They all went north and left the field half-picked. I've *never* known them leave meat.

what: Hew, on what your class tells him about you
text: And what's this, a censer? Gone _cold_ on you, and it'll want lighting again, though not off my kilns, I'd think, that'll be the Lantern's business. So you're church folk, then, or you robbed some.

what: Hew, on what your class tells him about you
text: And that thing in your hand's still ~humming~, I can hear it from here, so mind you don't point it my way. I don't hold with it, sparks out of sticks and all that, but I'll not leave you lying here over it, I suppose.

what: Hew, on what your class tells him about you
text: Bow's not broken, that's something, though the string's had a soaking. And this great grey lump's yours, I take it? The grass is dry under it, so it's been lying across your legs all night, and never a peep out of it with them at it over there.

what: Hew, on what your class tells him about you
text: Those are ^hunter's hands^ if ever I saw any, which is as well, I'd sooner you saw that lot coming a long way off. And I'll be a good way behind you when you do.

what: Hew, on what your class tells him about you
text: Hold on, two knives, and neither worn where a soldier would wear one. I'll keep a hand on my *purse*, if it's all the same to you, not that there's much in it, Wickhold owes me for four loads. And you keep both of yours where I can see them.

what: Hew, on what your class tells him about you
text: That's a soldier's arm on you, I've been round enough of them this morning to know. With the column, were you? No, don't answer, you'll only have to think about it.

what: Hew, before the parry lesson
text: Now, this big one breaks a guard like kindling. I turned over a few on that field who'd held theirs up and waited, shields _split down the middle_. You want to *meet* it, I'd say, not wait for it.

what: Hew, when you get a lesson right
Hew, when you get a lesson right
text: Oh, that's good, do it like that.

text: Wait here, stray, I'll go round the back.

what: Hew, cut off
Hew screaming as the Stoker takes him
text: Get off! Get *off* me! Aah! AAAH!

what: Hew, before a lesson your class does its own way
text: Three of them, and you'll not stand toe to toe with three, not with those little things, so you get yourself round the *back* of one. I expect you know how, I expect you've had a fair bit of practice.

what: Hew, before a lesson your class does its own way
text: Four of them bunched round my kiln like they're warming their hands. If that thing does what I think it does, you'll let it build a good while first, I'd have thought. Don't tell me how, mind, I'd sooner not know.

what: Hew, before a lesson your class does its own way
text: Two more out of the trees, and fresh ones. Now, you're the size for it, I'd say, and there's crates come off those carts, so pick one up and throw it at them. Or get round the back of one while it's got its head down and pick *it* up instead. They hate that, I've noticed.

what: Hew, before a lesson your class does its own way
text: Three coming up past the kilns, and slow about it, so there's time to draw it all the way back, and you take it, mind. I've seen half a draw go into one of them, and all it did was make it *cross*.

what: Hew, before a lesson your class does its own way
text: Now, this big one breaks a guard like kindling, and you've not got much guard to break, so you wait for it, wait, and be gone *just* as it comes down, and then it's yours while it gets over the surprise.

what: Hew, when you go down in the wood
text: Up you get, and spit that dirt out.

what: Hew, when you go down in the wood
text: Not yet, stray, I've enough to burn as it is.

what: Hew, when you go down in the wood
text: Have a breather, then go at it again, ~properly~ this time.

what: Hew, waking you on the battlefield (one box per tap)
text: Oh, you're ^breathing^. That's *one*, then, out of the whole field, and I've been round every one of them since first light. Give me a moment getting down, these knees pop like green wood in a kiln.

what: Hew, waking you on the battlefield (one box per tap)
text: Anything broken? Move your toes for me. Good, *all ten*, I counted. Soldier or thief or whatever you are, and that's none of my business, they've had your boots off you all the same.

what: Hew, waking you on the battlefield (one box per tap)
text: ^Have mine^, go on. They've been resoled twice and they let the wet in at the left heel, I won't lie to you, but it's them or bare feet, and I've *seen* your feet.

what: Hew, waking you on the battlefield (one box per tap)
text: Up you come, then, ~slowly~, there you are. Lean on me as much as you like, I've carried cordwood heavier than you up that hill and it never once thanked me.

what: Hew, on the card that asks you to walk
text: Have a little walk about first, stray, get the blood back in your legs, and mind the carts, they're still _burning_.

what: Narration: coming round after the Stoker knocks you down
text: You come round on the rise with a mouthful of ash, and it's still down there by the cordwood, _waiting_ for you.

what: Narration: cutting the javelin out of the Stoker
text: There's something hard under its breastbone, grown in like a knot in oak, and it takes Hew's poker and most of what you've got left to lever it out. It's a javelin, haft and all, longer than the wound it came out of, and ~warm~.

what: Narration: leaving the wood for Wickhold
text: The wood thins and then gives out, and there's a road, and at the end of it walls, with a ~glow~ over them that isn't the moon. Your left foot is wet through at the heel, just as Hew said it would be.
